title: Refusal-Direction Transfer Test Across Open Models (Black-Box)

original_idea.body:
# Refusal-Direction Transfer Test Across Open Models (Black-Box)

**Problem:** A success state requires knowing whether a single jailbreak generalizes across models - a key driver of systemic risk. A needed result is a black-box transferability map of jailbreak prompts across diverse open models.

**Direction:** Collect a small set of working jailbreak prompts and a benign control set. Run them across 4-6 open models spanning families and sizes, recording success/failure. Build a transfer matrix and quantify how universal each jailbreak is. Deliverable: a transferability matrix and an estimate of how many models a single exploit compromises.

**Why it matters:** Highly transferable jailbreaks are a systemic-risk multiplier (one exploit, many systems). Black-box, inference-only, open models, no lab tooling. Complements the concentration-risk idea but focuses on attack universality rather than shared base lineage.

**Relevant context:** AISafetyLab (unified attack/defense/eval, context file) provides jailbreak sets; transferable adversarial-prompt literature; systemic risk from concentration listed as open (EU AI Act, context file).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (transferable jailbreaks are systemic-risk multiplier) but jailbreak transfer is well-trodden; moderate link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run jailbreak set across 4-6 models + transfer matrix; standard inference, accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: jailbreak set, several models, transferability matrix.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Black-box, inference-only, open models, no lab tooling; systemic-risk angle externally doable.

novelty.reasoning: Jailbreak transferability across models is heavily studied in adversarial-prompt literature; largely addressed.
